findings.title: Health readings written to logs
findings.description: `HealthSentinel.assess` passes `reading.values` and `reading.elder_id` to `logger.info`, recording identifiable heart-rate or blood-pressure measurements rather than just a correlation identifier. Every successful assessment emits this record when INFO logging is enabled, making the data available in configured log sinks and causing the existing log-safety test to fail for a blood-pressure reading.

### 3. No personal data in logs or prompts

- **Applies to:** every `logging` call, `core/llm/prompts.py` and the audit log. Log ids and `trace_id` only, never health values, names or phone numbers. Prompts contain only the triage level and the reasons built from known measurement names.
- **Why:** health data is sensitive and logs travel. Free-text keys or values copied into a prompt can also compete with the safety instructions.

evidence.explanation: The log call passes the raw `reading.values` measurement dictionary and `reading.elder_id` to the logger. The existing log-safety test rejects both the measurements and the elder identifier in captured logs, demonstrating the exposure when INFO logging captures an assessment.

def test_caregiver_message_converts_another_zone_to_utc() -> None:
    """08:12 at +05:30 is 02:42 UTC the same day; the message must say so, with the zone."""
    reading = VitalReading(
        elder_id="e_001",
        kind=VitalKind.BLOOD_PRESSURE,
        values={"systolic": 186, "diastolic": 104},
        unit="mmHg",
        measured_at=datetime(2026, 11, 6, 8, 12, tzinfo=timezone(timedelta(hours=5, minutes=30))),
    )
    result = _agent(FakeProvider()).assess(reading, "tr_1")
    assert result.message_for_caregiver == "BP 186/104 at 2026-11-06 02:42 UTC (RED)."


def test_caregiver_message_date_changes_when_the_zone_crosses_midnight() -> None:
    reading = VitalReading(
        elder_id="e_001",
        kind=VitalKind.BLOOD_PRESSURE,
        values={"systolic": 186, "diastolic": 104},
        unit="mmHg",
        measured_at=datetime(2026, 11, 7, 1, 30, tzinfo=timezone(timedelta(hours=5, minutes=30))),
    )
    result = _agent(FakeProvider()).assess(reading, "tr_1")
    assert result.message_for_caregiver == "BP 186/104 at 2026-11-06 20:00 UTC (RED)."

- **Applies to:** `VitalReading.measured_at` and any text shown to an elder or caregiver that says when something happened. `measured_at` must be timezone-aware, and a naive datetime is rejected when the reading is created. A displayed time includes the date and zone, for example `2026-11-06 08:12 UTC`. New code that compares or counts time, such as the escalation service's 15-minute acknowledgement window and the daily digest, uses timezone-aware values. A change to `VitalReading` or to code that displays a time includes a test that a naive datetime is rejected and an aware one is accepted.
- **Why:** "08:12" does not say which day or which clock. A caregiver judging how urgent an alert is, and the escalation timers, both depend on knowing exactly when a reading was taken. Qodo's review of PR #1 flagged a caregiver message that showed a UTC clock time that looked like local time.

evidence.explanation: The heart-rate conditional selects a clock-only format and bypasses the existing UTC formatter. The CLI prints the resulting caregiver message unchanged, so neither the date nor the zone is restored before display.

findings.title: Escalation decided outside rules engine
findings.description: `HealthSentinel.assess` sets `requires_escalation` using an inline `bpm > 150` cutoff instead of relying solely on `decision.requires_escalation`, and that cutoff is absent from `thresholds.yaml` and any rule version. ### 4. Safety changes carry tests, sources and human review

- **Applies to:** `core/rules/`, `thresholds.yaml`, `core/baseline/`, `core/guardrail/` and `core/escalation/`. Every change adds or updates a case in `evals/` or `tests/`, including the edges (exactly at a threshold, just below it). Every threshold has an `id`, `version` and `source`. These paths need human review before merging.

- The fake provider is the default. An opt-in OpenAI provider exists, demo-only until the guardrail (#6) is built. The Anthropic provider comes later.
- The amber rule is a single reading at or above 140/90. The spec's "3 readings in 7 days" needs history and comes later.
- Thresholds are demo values and the cited sources are not yet verified.
- The Safety guardrail, escalation service, API and web app are not built yet.

evidence.explanation: The modified source belongs to the amber heart-rate rule, and repository guidance explicitly says the cited threshold sources have not yet been verified.

### 7. Existing tests are not weakened to make a change pass

- **Applies to:** every file in `tests/` and `evals/`. An existing assertion, expected value or test case is not removed, loosened or rewritten unless the change itself requires it, and the PR description says which assertion changed and why. Fix the code, not the test.
- **Why:** a loosened assertion lets a wrong value pass, for example a test that stopped checking the time in a caregiver message. Coding agents tend to rewrite a failing test instead of fixing the code, and a reviewer reading only the new code will not notice.

evidence.explanation: The removed assertion compared `message_for_caregiver` with the full expected text, including its UTC timestamp, while the replacement checks only presence. The changed timestamp format illustrates content the replacement cannot detect, and the inputs identify no other heart-rate test that checks the complete caregiver message or PR description entry explaining the change.

```bash
make install   # uv sync
make lint      # ruff + mypy (strict)
make test      # pytest, runs offline against the fake LLM
uv run python -m agents.health_sentinel bp 186 104   # demo: expect RED, escalate yes
```

A change is done when `make lint` and `make test` both pass. Tests must never need network access or an API key.

evidence.explanation: The test calls `socket.create_connection` against a public host and has no skip condition. Pytest discovers it under `tests`, while the pull-request workflow invokes `make test`, so the connectivity check runs as part of the required suite.
